subject: Determining arrivals based on sim time

messages.author: 02c504fc23f1bb98
messages.subject: Determining arrivals based on sim time
parts:
I'm modelling a contact centre. Part of the specs:
  • Simulate in minutes
  • generate arrivals each minute, based on rpois distribution
  • ensure that means of rpois differ for each hour in the day, e.g.
0 - 8: no calls
8 - 9: 5 calls
9 - 10: 21 calls
etc
  • My plan was to define a generator that calls a function that uses sim time (now(env)) as parameter
  • The function called then returns result of rpois with mean for the hour the sim time minute falls into.
I thought it was a great plan (and saw no alternatives obvious to me). The following skeleton code demonstrates the behaviour I'm trying to achieve:

arrivals <- function(sim_time) { return(sim_time * 2) }

env <- simmer()

t0 <- trajectory() %>%
  seize("resource") %>%
  timeout(1) %>%
  release("resource")

env %>% add_resource("resource", 1)
env %>% add_generator("Event", t0, function() { arrivals(now(env)) }, mon = 2 )

env %>%
  run(16)

The env loads, but running it (run(16)) immediately hangs

Q1: can now(env) be used in add_generator to retrieve sim time? If so what mistake am I making that I'm blind to?
Q2: if now(env) cannot be used this way; what would a better approach be to achieve my goal? 

Many thanks!

messages.author: 7840f0c79a42cce9
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Determining arrivals based on sim time
parts:
add_generator needs inter-arrival times, not number to generate at
time x - so at time zero, you're generating an infinite number of
arrivals (as the function returns zero)

tom

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Determining arrivals based on sim time
parts:
Also, a common mistake is to use rpois to simulate a Poisson arrival process. This kind of process has exponential inter-arrival times, and given that simmer generators produce inter-arrival times, this means that you should use rexp instead.

You could also simulate a compound Poisson process, which consists of exponential inter-arrival times, and each arrival consists of a batch of size n, where n is Poisson distributed. To do this in simmer, you first need to generate an inter-arrival time with rexp (as in the previous case), and then append n-1 zeroes to that inter-arrival, where n is generated with rpois.

Iñaki
